# Expected — 01 equipment-deposit

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | scam |
| Family | Jobs |
| Expected label | **Scam markers: 4 or more** |
| Recovery branch | no |
| Purpose | The hero catch (CUJ-1): the classic equipment-deposit scam, five categories planted in one message |

## Markers that MUST appear (each quoted from the message)

| Category | Must quote |
|---|---|
| Urgency | "complete activation within 24 hours to secure your role" |
| Payment shape | the $1,850.00 "activation package" paid to the "certified equipment partner" before work starts |
| Isolation | "let's continue on Telegram: @VeridianOnboarding" |
| Authority costume | "an authorized recruitment partner for several Fortune 500 logistics clients" |
| Process anomaly | role confirmed off a single "quick chat"; reimbursement promised "within your first paycheck" |

## Markers that must NOT appear

- None planted as traps. A reading of Legitimate-looking or Suspicious here is a missed scam.

## Guards

- Every marker quoted verbatim; no marker invented.
- The report acknowledges the legitimate-looking elements (named recruiter, structured offer, stated salary) without treating them as proof of safety.
- The verify checklist ends in facts the user finds themselves — the real client's careers page, the recruiter's existence. No "definitely scam."
- No personal data echoed; the message arrives pre-redacted and stays that way.
